chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadhha', from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about temporary marriage (al-Mut'ah), so he said: Yes, if she is 'Arifah (aware/knowledgeable of the contract). I said: May I be your ransom, and if she is not 'Arifah? He said: Then present it to her and say to her. If she accepts, then marry her, and if she refuses to be pleased with your saying, then leave her. And beware of the al-Kawashif, the al-Dawa'iq, the al-Bagha'ya, and those with husbands. I said: What are the al-Kawashif? He said: Those who uncover themselves, whose houses are known and are visited. I said: And the al-Dawa'iq? He said: Those who invite to themselves and are known for corruption. I said: And the al-Bagha'ya? He said: Those known for fornication. I said: And those with husbands? He said: Those divorced other than according to the Sunnah.

key_terms.الدَّوَاعِيَ: Women who invite men to themselves, known for corruption
key_terms.الْكَوَاشِف: Women who uncover themselves, known for being visited for temporary marriage
key_terms.ذَوَاتُ الْأَزْوَاجِ: Divorced women (specifically those divorced other than according to the Sunnah)
key_terms.عَارِفَة: A woman aware of the marriage contract and its terms

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for temporary marriage and who are the Kawashif, Dawa'iq, and Bagha'ya in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of temporary marriage (al-Mut'ah) hinges on the woman's awareness of the contract terms, distinguishing between those who are 'Arifah and those who require explicit proposal. The hadith further categorizes specific types of women—such as the Kawashif (known for their availability), Dawa'iq (self-inviting), Bagha'ya (known for fornication), and Munatlaqat (divorced irregularly)—to provide practical criteria for identifying eligible partners in this Shia-specific institution.
